title: Behavior-flag deprecation rehearsal and repair plan for streaming + toolcalls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Run a controlled, observable rehearsal of a planned behavior-flag deprecation that affects streaming responses and tool/function-calling code paths. The goal is to validate that existing clients (SDKs, older agents) will continue to behave acceptably when a behavior flag is removed and that our automated repair/rollback strategies (replay, canary rollback and compatibility adapter) will operate correctly. This ticket coordinates the rehearsal run, the backcompat test-suite sweep, and a small set of remediation automations (hot-fix API-level shim and a retry-fanout policy).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible rehearsal run that exercises both streaming-only flows and streaming-with-toolcall flows against a shadow traffic slice (1% of prod) without impacting production SLOs
Automated backcompat test-suite (see test_plan) passes against latest SDKs and two previous minor versions with no more than 2% functional regressions for structured-output parsability
Rollback automation triggers within 60s of breach of canary thresholds and successfully restores behavior-flag state or enables compatibility adapter
Dashboards show telemetry for schema-violation-rate, toolcall-failure-rate, stream-drop-rate, p95 latency, and end-user error-rate during the run
Runbook with postmortem checklist, required follow-ups, and a patch plan is published to Confluence and linked in artifacts
test_plan: Unit/regression: Extend compat unit tests to assert both streaming chunk semantics and final structured payload schema under flag-on and flag-off modes
Integration: Run SDK matrix (JS, Python, Go) against a replay harness that replays historical traffic for streaming+tool calls (last 7 days of production traffic anonymized)
Shadow-run: Route 1% of live requests to a shadow cluster with the flag removed; compare responses with golden baseline and run fuzzy diff metrics (semantic-equivalence + token-delta thresholds)

End-to-end: Simulate 5 client apps (chat, code-assistant, email-summarizer, search-reranker, orchestration agent) for behavioral regressions related to tool invocation ordering and structured-output parsing
Chaos: Introduce KV-cache staleness and artificially slowed kernels in the shadow cluster to validate graceful fallback and repair automations
rollout_steps: 1) Prep: Merge compatibility adapters and hot-fix shims to canary branch (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14823)
2) Dry-run: Execute replay harness locally against canary-runtime with instrumentation enabled; run automated post-run analyzer
3) Shadow: Enable flag-off on shadow cluster and route 1% prod traffic for 72 hours; monitor telemetry and alerts
4) Canary: If shadow run meets thresholds, toggle flag-off in a single region for 0.5% of traffic with circuit-breaker thresholds; observe for 24 hours
5) Scale canary and evaluate until safe to fully remove flag; if any threshold breached, run automatic rollback and open incident timeline
mitigation_plan: If the rehearsal or canary breaches thresholds (see telemetry), three remediation actions are available in order: 1) activate compatibility adapter (automatic patch that rewrites streaming frames to legacy schema), 2) flip behavior-flag back on globally via remote-config with immediate prioritization, 3) deploy emergency hotfix to SDKs and issue coordinated client patch notes. The operation runbook includes precise thresholds, play-by-play commands, and mapped on-call owners.
telemetry: stream_drop_rate (% of sessions with truncated streaming chunks)
